mission.summary_text: The Apollo 11 lunar module ascent stage, the first crewed vehicle to lift off from the Moon.
mission.abandonment_reason: Left in lunar orbit after the Apollo 11 rendezvous; the ascent stage was never recovered.

facts.fact_text: Eagle lifted off from the Moon on 21 July 1969 and returned Armstrong and Aldrin to Columbia in lunar orbit.
After docking, the ascent stage was jettisoned and left in lunar orbit.

media.title: Astronaut Buzz Aldrin beside the Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle
Apollo Lunar Module 3D model

mission.summary_text: A robotic lunar lander visited by the Apollo 12 crew, providing the first on-site inspection of another spacecraft on the Moon.
mission.abandonment_reason: Left on the Moon after its mission; Apollo 12 removed parts for study.

facts.fact_text: Surveyor 3 landed in Oceanus Procellarum on 20 April 1967.
The Apollo 12 crew visited the lander in November 1969 and returned parts to Earth for analysis.

media.title: Surveyor 3 and the Apollo 12 lunar module on the Moon

mission.summary_text: A Mars rover exploring Jezero Crater and caching samples for a possible return to Earth.

facts.fact_text: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on 18 February 2021.
The rover is collecting rock and soil samples for a possible future Mars Sample Return mission.

media.title: Perseverance's selfie with Ingenuity

mission.summary_text: The first successful long-lived lander on Mars, and the first to return images from the surface.
mission.abandonment_reason: Contact was lost in November 1982; the lander remains on Mars.

facts.fact_text: Viking 1 landed in Chryse Planitia on 20 July 1976.
The lander returned images and weather data until November 1982.

media.title: Mars surface near the Viking Lander 1 footpad

mission.summary_text: A 1958 engineering satellite and the oldest human-made object still in orbit.
mission.abandonment_reason: Transmissions ended in 1964; the satellite remains in orbit.

facts.fact_text: Vanguard 1 was launched on 17 March 1958.
It stopped transmitting in 1964 and remains the oldest human-made object in orbit.

media.title: Waiting for the Vanguard 1 launch at Cape Canaveral

mission.summary_text: A space telescope that has observed the universe from low Earth orbit since 1990.

facts.fact_text: Hubble was deployed from Space Shuttle Discovery on 25 April 1990.
Five servicing missions between 1993 and 2009 repaired and upgraded the telescope.

media.title: Hubble Space Telescope above Space Shuttle Discovery's payload bay during STS-31

mission.summary_text: A spacecraft that toured Jupiter and Saturn and is now in interstellar space.

facts.fact_text: Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980.
It crossed the heliopause in August 2012 and is now in interstellar space.

media.title: Voyager spacecraft artist concept
Voyager 3D model

mission.summary_text: The first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter, now leaving the Solar System.
mission.abandonment_reason: Contact was lost in January 2003; the spacecraft is coasting out of the Solar System.

facts.fact_text: Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and the first to fly past Jupiter, in December 1973.
NASA lost contact with Pioneer 10 in January 2003.

media.title: Pioneer 10 and 11 spacecraft
Pioneer 10 3D model

mission.summary_text: A Mars Exploration Rover that far outlived its 90-day design life and found evidence of ancient water.
mission.abandonment_reason: Contact was lost after a planet-wide dust storm in June 2018; the rover remains in Perseverance Valley.

facts.fact_text: Opportunity landed in Meridiani Planum on 25 January 2004.
The rover operated for more than 14 years and last contacted Earth in June 2018.

media.title: Mars rover Opportunity at rock abrasion target Potts
Opportunity 3D model
media.credit: NASA 3D Resources — Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER-B)

mission.summary_text: The first lunar roving vehicle, used by the Apollo 15 crew to explore the Hadley-Apennine region.
mission.abandonment_reason: Left on the Moon at the Hadley-Apennine landing site.

facts.fact_text: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was first used on Apollo 15 in July 1971.
Astronauts David Scott and James Irwin drove it 27.8 km across the Hadley-Apennine region.

media.title: Astronaut James Irwin works at the Lunar Roving Vehicle during Apollo 15

mission.summary_text: A Mars lander that studied the planet's interior and detected marsquakes.
mission.abandonment_reason: The mission ended in December 2022 after dust reduced the lander's power; it remains on Mars.

facts.fact_text: InSight landed in Elysium Planitia on 26 November 2018.
Its seismometer detected more than 1,300 marsquakes before the mission ended in December 2022.

media.title: Artist concept of the InSight lander on Mars
InSight lander 3D model

mission.summary_text: The first United States space station, occupied by three crews in 1973–74.
mission.abandonment_reason: Abandoned after three crewed visits; it reentered on 11 July 1979.

facts.fact_text: Skylab was launched on 14 May 1973 as the United States' first space station.
It reentered Earth's atmosphere over the Indian Ocean and Western Australia on 11 July 1979.

media.title: View of the Skylab space station cluster against black sky
Skylab 3D model

mission.summary_text: The second crewed lunar module, which landed in Oceanus Procellarum and visited Surveyor 3.
mission.abandonment_reason: The descent stage remains in Oceanus Procellarum; the ascent stage was deliberately crashed into the Moon after docking.

facts.fact_text: Intrepid landed in Oceanus Procellarum on 19 November 1969, the second crewed lunar landing.
The crew walked to Surveyor 3 and returned parts of the lander to Earth for study.
After docking, the ascent stage was deliberately crashed into the Moon; the descent stage remains at the site.

media.title: Apollo 12 astronaut Alan Bean beside the TV camera near Surveyor Crater

mission.summary_text: The lunar module that landed at Hadley-Apennine and carried the first Lunar Roving Vehicle.
mission.abandonment_reason: The descent stage remains at Hadley-Apennine; the ascent stage was deliberately crashed into the Moon.

facts.fact_text: Falcon landed in the Hadley-Apennine region on 30 July 1971.
It carried the first Lunar Roving Vehicle, which the crew drove 27.8 km.
The descent stage remains at Hadley-Apennine; the ascent stage was crashed into the Moon.

media.title: Apollo 15 Lunar Module Falcon before ascent stage liftoff

relations.note: Falcon carried and deployed the first Lunar Roving Vehicle.

mission.summary_text: The last lunar module to land humans on the Moon, in the Taurus-Littrow valley.
mission.abandonment_reason: The descent stage remains at Taurus-Littrow; the ascent stage was deliberately crashed into the Moon.

facts.fact_text: Challenger landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley on 11 December 1972.
It was the last lunar module to land humans on the Moon.
The descent stage remains at Taurus-Littrow; the ascent stage was crashed into the Moon.

media.title: Apollo 17 Lunar Module Challenger lifts off from Taurus-Littrow

mission.summary_text: The last Lunar Roving Vehicle, left parked in the Taurus-Littrow valley.
mission.abandonment_reason: LRV-3 remains parked at Taurus-Littrow, left behind when the crew returned to Earth.

facts.fact_text: LRV-3 was driven 35.9 km across the Taurus-Littrow valley in December 1972.
Apollo 17 was the last crewed lunar landing, leaving LRV-3 as the last rover on the Moon.
LRV-3 remains parked at Taurus-Littrow, left behind when the crew returned to Earth.

media.title: Close-up of the Apollo 17 lunar roving vehicle at Taurus-Littrow

mission.summary_text: The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune, now in interstellar space.

facts.fact_text: Voyager 2 launched on 20 August 1977.
It is the only spacecraft to fly past Uranus and Neptune.
It crossed the heliopause in November 2018 and is now in interstellar space.

media.title: Voyager 2 spacecraft instruments

mission.summary_text: The first spacecraft to fly past Saturn, now coasting out of the Solar System.
mission.abandonment_reason: Contact was lost in September 1995; the spacecraft is coasting out of the Solar System.

facts.fact_text: Pioneer 11 launched on 6 April 1973.
It was the first spacecraft to fly past Saturn, in September 1979.
NASA lost contact with Pioneer 11 in September 1995.

media.title: Pioneer 10 and 11 spacecraft

mission.summary_text: The Pluto flyby spacecraft, now exploring the Kuiper Belt.

facts.fact_text: New Horizons launched on 19 January 2006.
It flew past Pluto on 14 July 2015 and Arrokoth on 1 January 2019.
It is still operating in the Kuiper Belt.

media.title: New Horizons sees Pluto

mission.summary_text: A Jupiter orbiter measuring the planet’s interior, magnetic field and atmosphere.

facts.fact_text: Juno launched on 5 August 2011 and entered Jupiter orbit on 4 July 2016.
It has measured Jupiter’s gravity, magnetic field and deep atmosphere.
Juno remains in orbit around Jupiter.

media.title: Juno approaches Jupiter (artist concept)

mission.summary_text: The first Mars Exploration Rover, which landed in Gusev Crater and far outlived its design life.
mission.abandonment_reason: Spirit became embedded in soft soil in 2009 and stopped communicating in 2010; it remains in Gusev Crater.

facts.fact_text: Spirit landed in Gusev Crater on 4 January 2004.
It became embedded in soft soil in 2009 and last communicated with Earth in March 2010.
It found evidence of ancient volcanic activity and hot springs at Gusev Crater.

media.title: Spirit stretches out its lander petals on Mars

mission.summary_text: A polar lander that confirmed water ice beneath the Martian surface.
mission.abandonment_reason: The lander went silent in November 2008 when winter darkness ended its solar power; it remains in the Arctic plain.

facts.fact_text: Phoenix landed in the Martian Arctic on 25 May 2008.
It confirmed water ice beneath the landing site and observed falling snow.
Its last contact was in November 2008, when winter darkness ended solar power.

media.title: Phoenix Mars Lander during spacecraft processing

mission.summary_text: A car-sized rover exploring Gale Crater and the habitability of ancient Mars.

facts.fact_text: Curiosity landed in Gale Crater on 6 August 2012.
It found ancient lake and stream deposits that could have supported microbial life.
Curiosity is still operating on Mars.

media.title: Curiosity drilling into its second rock target

mission.summary_text: The modular Soviet and Russian space station that hosted long-duration crews for 15 years.
mission.abandonment_reason: Mir was deorbited on 23 March 2001 and re-entered over the South Pacific; no intact station remains.

facts.fact_text: Mir was launched on 20 February 1986 and assembled in low Earth orbit.
It hosted record-long crew stays and international visitors, including NASA astronauts.
Mir was deliberately deorbited on 23 March 2001 and broke up over the South Pacific.

media.title: Mir space station seen from Space Shuttle Discovery during STS-63

mission.summary_text: A large European Earth-observation satellite that stopped communicating in 2012.
mission.abandonment_reason: Contact was lost in April 2012; Envisat remains in orbit as one of the largest derelict satellites.

facts.fact_text: Envisat launched on 1 March 2002 into a Sun-synchronous orbit.
Its radar and optical instruments monitored land, oceans, ice and the atmosphere for a decade.
Contact was lost in April 2012; the satellite remains in orbit.

media.title: Envisat radar data used to map the 2011 Tohoku earthquake

mission.summary_text: An Earth-observation satellite that operated for 29 years, far beyond its design life.
mission.abandonment_reason: Landsat 5 was decommissioned in June 2013 and remains in orbit without propellant.

facts.fact_text: Landsat 5 launched on 1 March 1984.
It operated for 29 years, far beyond its three-year design life.
Landsat 5 was decommissioned in June 2013 and remains in orbit.

media.title: Landsat view of Las Vegas, Nevada
